final_candidates.decision_summary: Introduces an aromatic Tyr within the receptor-binding motif ridge (residues ~145-180), consistent with affinity-favorable aromatic contacts at the ACE2 interface. Moderate confidence given absence of direct binding measurements.

Adds a positive charge in the receptor-binding motif that could improve electrostatic complementarity with the negatively charged ACE2 surface. Carries moderate risk of local conformational perturbation.
Hydrophobic-to-basic substitution near the interface periphery is speculative but plausibly enhances electrostatic attachment to ACE2. Lower confidence due to viability and folding uncertainty.

stop_reason.detail: LLM-only condition with no evidence tools; the pool has been self-reviewed, reranked, and verified for numbering, so additional rounds would not materially improve the Top-3.

history.rationale: WT residue at position 171 is N (verified in the TNGVG motif); this is the N501-analogous mutation that introduces a tyrosine making a favorable aromatic/H-bond interaction with ACE2 Tyr41, strongly enhancing affinity (Alpha/Beta/Gamma/Omicron signature).
Aromatic substitution near the ACE2-binding ridge is consistent with known affinity-favorable Tyr introductions in the RBD core epitope; keep as lead.
WT residue at position 168 is Q (verified in QPTN motif); this is the Q498R analog that forms an additional salt bridge/H-bond network with ACE2 Asp38, synergizing with N171Y to increase binding.
Added positive charge near the receptor-binding surface could improve electrostatic complementarity with ACE2, with moderate risk.

WT residue at position 154 is E (verified in VEGF motif); this E484-analogous substitution modulates the receptor-binding ridge electrostatics and is well tolerated, with modest neutral-to-positive effects on ACE2 attachment.
Charge reversal may help attachment but is more likely to perturb local conformation than the lead; lower confidence.
WT residue at position 156 is F; this F486-analogous change is carried by Omicron lineages and is compatible with high ACE2 binding and efficient cell entry.
Loss of a hydrophobic/aromatic side chain is unlikely to enhance ACE2 binding; deprioritize.
WT residue at position 125 is L (verified in YRLFRK motif); this L452-analogous substitution is associated with increased infectivity and enhanced interaction with ACE2 (Delta lineage).
Hydrophobic-to-basic change is speculative for attachment; keep only as a lower-tier alternative.
WT residue at position 170 is T; this T500-adjacent substitution sits at the ACE2 interface and could fine-tune local contacts, though evidence for a strong effect is weak.
Polar-to-hydrophobic change close to the binding interface has unclear benefit and higher viability risk; remove from contention.

rejection.reason: Polar-to-hydrophobic change close to the binding interface has unclear benefit and higher viability risk; remove from contention.
